root_topic: Methods of Separation in Everyday Life

details: Handpicking: Used when unwanted impurities differ in size, shape, or color and are present in small quantities (e.g., stones from wheat).
Threshing: Process of beating harvested crop stalks to free grain seeds (manually or mechanically).
Winnowing: Separating lighter husk from heavier grain seeds using wind currents.
Sieving: Separating particles of different sizes using a perforated mesh screen (e.g., fine flour through sieve, bran remains).
experiments_or_examples: Winnowing grain mixture in wind; sieving flour and sand mixtures

details: Sedimentation: Heavier insoluble solid particles settle down at the bottom of a liquid mixture when left undisturbed.
Decantation: Gently pouring off the upper clear liquid layer without disturbing the settled sediment.
Filtration: Passing liquid containing insoluble solid through a porous filter paper/cloth; liquid passes as 'filtrate', solid remains as 'residue'.
experiments_or_examples: Purifying muddy water using filter paper cone in glass funnel

details: Evaporation: Heating solution to vaporize liquid solvent, leaving dissolved solid behind (e.g., obtaining sea salt).
Churning / Centrifugation: Agitating milk/cream to separate lighter butter from heavy liquid buttermilk.
Magnetic Separation: Using magnets to attract and extract magnetic iron impurities from non-magnetic mixtures.
experiments_or_examples: Evaporating salt solution in a china dish; pulling iron filings from sand using a bar magnet
